I am an authorized representative requesting policy clarification regarding the Economic Mobility Pathways Pilot (EMPP).

As you know, individuals selected under the EMPP are processed through an economic immigration stream, rather than as protected persons under section 95 of the IRPA

My inquiry concerns individuals who have already landed in Canada and now hold permanent resident status obtained through the EMPP.

In traditional refugee protection cases, individuals are cautioned not to travel to their country of origin due to potential “re-

# availment” concerns. Given that EMPP participants are economic immigrants, I seek clarification on whether similar

restrictions or policy considerations apply once they hold permanent resident status in Canada.

Specifically, could IRCC confirm whether temporary travel to their country of nationality has any implications for their Canadian permanent resident status or for a pending or future citizenship application, assuming the individual continues to meet all residence and admissibility requirements.

This request is for policy clarification only and does not relate to any specific client file. If possible, please direct me to any Program Delivery Instructions or operational guidance that address these matters.

# Policy:

Conditions (eligibility requirements) applicable to foreign nationals except where they are an accompanying family member of a principal applicant on an application for permanent residence (for a permanent resident visa or applied to remain in Canada a permanent resident):

1. 1. The foreign national
i. i. Has made an application under the Act and has indicated a Canadian residence on the application; ii. ii. Has submitted to an Immigration Medical Examination that included a physical examination under paragraph 29(a) of the Regulations
a. a. Within the five years before the date the new application under the Act is submitted in the case of a foreign national who submits an application on or after the date this temporary public policy comes into effect, or
b. b. Within the five years before the coming into effect of this temporary public policy in the case of a foreign national whose application under the Act is pending on the date the public policy comes into effect, and
2. 2. The foreign national's most recent IME described in subsection 1(ii) was assessed and coded as:
i. i. M1: indicating they pose no danger to public health and public safety; ii. ii. M3: indicating they have a health condition present but are not expected to place an excessive demand on health or social services, unless the M3 has been assessed and identified as “TR only” or “EDE only”; or
iii. iii. M2 or M2/3: indicating they are a potential risk to public health, but they have complied with their requirement to report to provincial/territorial health authorities for medical surveillance, unless the M2 or M2/3 has been assessed and identified as “TR only” or “EDE only”. ***

As outlined under paragraph 133(1)(k) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), a sponsorship application will only be approved if, from the day the application was submitted until the day a decision is made on that application, a sponsor is not in receipt of social assistance for a reason other than disability.

any benefit in the form of money, goods or services provided to or on behalf of a person by a province under a program of social assistance, including a program of social assistance designated by a province to provide for basic requirements including food, shelter, clothing, fuel, utilities, household supplies, personal requirements and health care

If a sponsor is receiving social assistance for a reason other than disability, they will be found ineligible and the sponsorship application will be refused. Pursuant to R133(1)(g)(i), sponsors are also ineligible if a previously sponsored family member received social assistance or welfare while the undertaking was valid, until the full amount has been

Manitoba's Rent Assist program offers a monthly shelter benefit for people who receive Employment and Income Assistance (EIA) and have eligible housing costs to cover. This is considered EIA Rent Assist. The Rent Assist program also offers a monthly shelter benefit to people who are renting in the private market and are not receiving income

Both EIA Rent Assist and non-EIA Rent Assist are considered social assistance under the IRPR. Therefore, a sponsor

Under the IRPA and IRPR's sponsorship requirements, repayment of social assistance applies only when a previously sponsored family member receives social assistance during the undertaking period. In this case, if the sponsor himself received Rent Assist before submitting the sponsorship application, there is no requirement to repay the benefit for immigration purposes. However, whether the province of Manitoba requires repayment of Rent Assist is a matter of provincial policy. The client should confirm this directly with the province of Manitoba's Rent Assist program/office.

Good day, Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives Mailbox. Please note that this mailbox is intended for general guidance and does not provide responses to case-specific inquiries but have provided the following information as guidance. If you have case specific questions about a file, you are encouraged to submit the IRCC Web form. Please see our response to your question. *** Q1: Does a child of a protected person (18 years or older) attending high school require a study permit?

Response: When minor children reach the age of majority (18 or 19 years old, depending on the province or territory), they must apply for a study permit if they want to keep studying, unless another exemption applies.

Q2: If this child is required to apply for a permit for high school studies, can they continue to study while their application is in process (under maintained status), considering that they were already permitted to study without a permit prior to turning 18?

Response: If the child applies for a study permit before turning 18, they may remain in Canada while the application is processed. However, they must wait until the study permit is approved before continuing their studies after reaching the age of majority.

Q3: If the child is required to apply for a study permit, would they be required to meet all the requirements of a study permit, including financial requirements, as an international student?

Response: Financial requirements apply to all applicants unless exempted under the regulations (e.g., scenarios described in R215(1)(d) or (e)). Applicants should provide documentation demonstrating their ability to support themselves during their studies, unless they fall under one of the exemptions.

For more information, please visit IRCC webpages: Studying in Canada as a minor-Canada.ca Study permit: Who can study without a permit-Canada.ca Study permit: Get the right documents-Proof of financial support-Canada.ca

We trust that this information will assist you. ***

# Study permit invalidity

As per R222(1), a study permit will become invalid upon the first of the following days:

a. 90 days after the day the study permit holder completed their studies;
1. a.1) The day on which the permit holder is no longer enrolled at the DLI named in their permit, other than as a result of completing their studies;
b. The day on which the permit is cancelled under 222.7, 222.8 or R243.2; or
c. The day on which the permit expires.
As such, study permit holders must ensure that they apply for a new study permit

## in advance of their current study permit's expiration, according to the invalidity

provisions. If a study permit holder continues to study, despite the previous permit's invalidity, they are considered to be studying without authorization.

Thank you,

000056

# Bonjour,

Récemment, la situation suivante est arrivée à 3 de nos clients :

* Le client a déjà un dossier avec l'’IRCC, a un document d’immigration avec un IUC.
- * Il soumet une demande pour prolonger son statut en ligne.
- * La lettre de confirmation d’envoi de la demande de prolongation de statut qui est normalement générée automatiquement dans la prochaine heure n’est toujours pas au dossier après plusieurs jours d’attente.
- * Selon l’état du dossier en ligne, nous voyons qu'un nouveau numéro lUC est attribué à ce client.
- * Le client a donc maintenant une demande de prolongation de statut lié à un mauvais numéro d’IUC.
- * Il a de la difficulté à démontrer à son employeur, à la RAMQ et à d’autres institutions qu’il va pouvoir conserver son statut après expiration de son permis actuel.

Nous avons envoyé un formulaire web pour signaler cette erreur et demander à l’IRCC de fusionner les deux dossiers, pour que le client puisse avoir sa demande traitée dans le bon dossier individuel et ainsi avoir les données biométriques au dossier et ne pas avoir à resoumettre d’autres sous un nouveau lUC.

En revanche, nous n’avons pas eu de retour pour les formulaires web envoyés à part un accusé de réception automatisé. Nous sommes inquiets que ces requêtes ne soient pas traitées avant 200+ jours (délais moyens de traitement de prolongation de permis de travail) et alors notre client sera dans une situation très précaire sans preuve de conservation de statut.

Merci de nous guider sur quoi faire dans ce genre de situation et comment nous pourrions accélérer ce processus pour avoir les lettres de confirmation d’envoi rapidement.

Cordialement,

000058

Good day,

### Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives Mailbox.

Please note that this mailbox is intended for general guidance and does not provide responses to case-specific inquiries but have provided the following information as guidance. If you have case specific

### questions about a file, you are encouraged to submit the IRCC Web form.

Please see our response to your question. *** Marriages in which one or both spouses are not physically present are excluded for immigration purposes.

We can confirm that this includes a situation where both spouses are physically present at the same location in the presence of witnesses, but with the celebrant attending online. The ceremony takes place where the celebrant is located. Therefore, if the two parties to the marriage are not in the same location as the celebrant, the parties to the marriage are not physically present at the marriage ceremony within the meaning of R117(9)(c.1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). As a result, this would be considered an online marriage, excluded for immigrations purposes.

We hope you find this information useful.

Please see our response to your question. *** If a principal applicant under the Family Class or Spouse or Common-law Partner in Canada (SCLPC) Class wishes to change their non-accompanying dependent to accompanying after the permanent resident visa (PRV)/Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR) has been issued, they may submit a written request via the IRCC web form.

Submitting this request will require cancellation of the principal applicant's COPR, and they will not be able to travel to Canada using the existing COPR until processing related to the dependent is complete. After receiving the written request, IRCC will request the necessary forms and documents to process the dependent.

The dependent, principal applicant, and/or sponsor must provide the following (non-exhaustive list):

1. 1. Generic Application Form for Canada (IMM 0008)
3. 3. Proof of payment of the processing fees and, if applicable, biometrics fees
4. 4. Additional Family Information (IMM 5406) form
5. 5. Schedule A– Background/Declaration (IMM 5669) form, if applicable
7. 7. Complete the immigration medical examination
8. 8. A copy of the dependent's valid passport or travel document
9. 9. Police certificate(s), if applicable
## 10. 10. Any additional country specific requirements

before a final decision is rendered.

The applicant's eligihilty under C42 depend on whether the principal foreign national met all riteria at the tme of decision, which is: - sudving in a master's degree program of 16 monihs or longer-studying in a docioral degree program-participating in an eligible program, or-studying in one of the following professional degree programs at a umiversity As per the PD)1, client should be studying at an eligible program listed in the PD1. However, IRCC's Operational Manual for spouses or common-law partners of study permit holders under R205(c)(ii) – C42 provides the following transitional policy considerations:

Operational guidance: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-) bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign-workers/public-policy-competitiveness- economy/c42.html#extensions

“In limited circumstances, spouses of principal foreign nationals studying in the following programs may apply for a work permit renewal under the criteria that were in place when they received their current work permit. This applies to spouses of principal foreign nationals studying in

- master's programs of less than 16 months, or
- college and undergraduate programs The spouse must be residing in Canada and be requesting an open work permit renewal for a duration that aligns with, and does not exceed, the principal foreign national's existing study authorization.
